name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset of 108,249 real-world images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. The dataset connects language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations and canonicalizes objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to WordNet synsets.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The first release uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. Workers created region descriptions by drawing bounding boxes and writing descriptions, then extracted objects and grounded them with bounding boxes, added attributes and relationships to form region graphs, wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs, verified annotations, and validated WordNet canonicalizations. The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation, with approximately 800,000 HITs launched.
rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The images are all 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users. Raw text data include freeform worker-generated region descriptions and question-answer pairs.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multiple descriptions referring to the same object were merged through co-reference chains. Scene graphs were created by combining region graphs and merging objects from different graphs when their bounding boxes had overlap over union of 0.8, with worker confirmation before merging. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets, using heuristics, hand-crafted mapping rules, and worker verification.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To collect diverse region descriptions, BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 were enforced against previously written image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions. Bounding boxes were required to satisfy coverage, and for objects also quality, with a relaxed four-pixel tolerance. Stanford dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for workers. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs. Attributes were normalized based on morphology, and relationships were mapped using WordNet sentence frames while ignoring prepositions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers. For region descriptions, workers drew three bounding boxes and wrote three descriptions per image, and the process repeated with new workers until 50 region descriptions were collected per image, while encouraging diversity. For objects, workers extracted all objects from each description and drew bounding boxes around them. For attributes and relationships, workers were shown a region description and its extracted objects and asked to add attributes to objects or connect object pairs with relationships, forming region graphs. For question answering, workers wrote freeform and region-based QA pairs following rules to start with one of the Ws, avoid ambiguity and speculation, and ensure questions were precise and image-grounded. Verification used majority voting for all components except objects, where rapid judgments were used. Canonicalization mappings to WordNet were also verified by workers choosing among five synset options.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using majority voting and rapid judgments. All components except objects were verified by three unique workers, and an annotation was added if at least two of three workers judged it factually correct. Rapid judgments were used for object verification to increase speed. Canonicalization mappings were sent to workers along with the top four alternative synsets so workers could verify or change the mapping.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Region descriptions: 50 per image; verification for most annotations: 3 workers per annotation; freeform QA: 8 QA pairs per image task; each image has on average 17 QA pairs and at least one question of each type.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% were from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries. The majority were between 25 and 34 years old. The youngest contributor was 18 and the oldest was 68. Gender split was 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools (Stanford CoreNLP)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the first release of the Visual Genome dataset and notes that crowdsourcing strategies were deployed in the ongoing effort of collecting the dataset. Further visualizations, API, and additional information can be found online. No explicit maintenance or deprecation policy is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator geography, age, and gender were collected and reported.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable training and benchmarking of the next generation of computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, with applications such as image search, question answering, robotic interactions, semantic image retrieval, dense image captioning, and image understanding.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports such as skiing and surfboarding are overrepresented due to a bias in the image set. The paper also notes that common visual concepts like 'blue sky' could dominate descriptions without diversity controls, and that previous direct scene-graph collection led workers to annotate easy, frequently occurring relationships like wearing(man, shirt).
rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Some descriptions contain no objects and therefore have no region graphs. The dataset's images are somewhat biased toward people, and certain sports are overrepresented. The paper also notes that current models perform poorly on several tasks using the dataset, illustrating difficulty of complex image reasoning, but does not provide explicit non-recommended uses.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is presented as a comprehensive dataset for training and benchmarking computer vision models. Explicit use cases include training and benchmarking for comprehensive scene understanding, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, and semantic image retrieval.
